title: Maximum Total Sum with Threshold Constraints
summary: Given two integer arrays, nums and threshold, both of length n, repeatedly select an index i where threshold[i] is less than or equal to the current step.
statement: Given two integer arrays, nums and threshold, both of length n, repeatedly select an index i where threshold[i] is less than or equal to the current step. Add nums[i] to the total sum, mark i as used, and increment the step. The process ends when no such index exists. Return the highest possible total sum.
constraints: nums and threshold have equal length up to 100,000 and all nums are positive.
At step one and later, choose one unused index whose threshold is at most the current step; stop when none is available.
hints: Choosing a task always advances the step, so among currently eligible tasks only its value affects optimality.
Sort indices by threshold, add newly eligible values to a max-heap, and take the largest each step.
Stop exactly when the heap is empty before another threshold is unlocked.
An exchange argument replaces any smaller chosen eligible task with the heap maximum without changing future eligibility and never lowers the score.
editorial: An exchange argument replaces any smaller chosen eligible task with the heap maximum without changing future eligibility and never lowers the score.

tests.explanation: The best eligible choices score 10, then 6, then 1 before the process blocks, totaling seventeen.
No task is eligible at step one, so the score is zero.
